newsitem.title: UK: U.K. 3rd qtr cocoa grind jumps 42 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: U.K. 3rd qtr cocoa grind jumps 42 pct on year.

text.p: The U.K. third quarter 1996 cocoa grind rose sharply by 41.9 percent to 48,855 tonnes when compared with the same period in 1995, the Biscuit, Cake, Chocolate and Confectionery Alliance (BCCCA) said on Friday.
The result compares with expectations the grind would rise by up to 10 percent in the quarter from the year before.
Earlier this week some industry sources forecast the UK grind would leap by 20 percent or more but the estimates were conditional.
The grind is believed to have been partly helped by the resumption of production at one major grinder. The year-ago grindings, the worst quarter in 1995, were affected by the closure of the plant.

The BCCCA said the third quarter grind represented an increase of 9.7 percent over the second quarter of 1996 when the total grindings were 44,535 tonnes. On Friday the Netherlands also reported a higher-than-expected third quarter grind of 99,549 tonnes, up 16.69 percent from the third quarter of 1995.
Cocoa grindings are considered a major indication of consumption.
